rows.behavior: Sign-in, sessions, roles and the pages each role gets

claims.claim: A password needs at least 12 characters
A user with no password cannot sign in
A session lasts FIRSTCALL_SESSION_DAYS days, default 7
Setting a password ends the user's other sessions
Sign-in allows FIRSTCALL_SIGNIN_RATE_PER_MINUTE tries, default 10
The sign-in limit applies per client address and per email
Team members get Pool and My leads
Monitors and admins get Unassigned, Waiting longest and the tray
Admins get Users
Everyone gets Inbox and Alerts on this device
Admins add, edit roles and teams, set passwords and deactivate on the Users page
Deactivating ends sessions and returns open leads to their pools
Removing someone from a team returns their open leads there to its pool
Salespeople see their teams' pools and their own leads; team leads see every lead in their teams; monitors and admins see the whole org
user add and user password create the first admin; the password is prompted

rows.behavior: Claiming: first claim wins, members only, owner and team lead actions

claims.claim: Every member of the team is alerted for a new lead
A lost claim reads 'Already claimed by a teammate'
The API answers a lost claim with 'already claimed'
Only a member of the lead's team can claim
Claim needs a team, so Unassigned leads are placed first
The owner can release
A team lead or admin can return
A team lead or admin can move a lead to another team
Reassign goes only to an active member of the lead's team
Lists refresh every 15 seconds while visible
The first claim wins; a loser sees Already claimed by a teammate

rows.behavior: Wait, urgency labels and escalation count business minutes from the current pool stay

claims.claim: Every return to a pool starts a new stay
A rescue starts the stay at the rescue
The wait counts from pool_since, or arrival
A team wait is business minutes
An Unassigned wait is wall-clock minutes
Waiting from 5 minutes
Late at the team's first escalation level
Very late at the team's second level
Unassigned Late at 15
Default minutes 15 and 60
Escalation counts from the stay
Unassigned escalation counts wall-clock minutes
Team config keys team_unclaimed and team_still_unclaimed
Team escalation minutes come from the team's config
Each escalation is stored once per lead, level and stay
A team whose config does not read is logged and skipped
Time to claim is set once, at the first claim
Time to claim counts from arrival
Labels use the escalation minutes, so Late matches escalation
The Waiting longest page lists Late and Very late leads, then escalations
The escalation log is for monitors and admins
The timer counts business minutes from when the lead last entered a pool

claims.claim: Monitors are alerted when a lead arrives in Unassigned
A monitor or admin places a lead
Only monitors and admins use the tray
A rescue rereads stored bytes and the stored model answer, no new call
A rescued message is treated as a lead
The history records the rescue and who did it

rows.behavior: Alerts: inbox digests, retries, the send-time access check and the allowlist

claims.claim: Back in a pool, placed or moved alerts the new pool
A reassigned lead alerts the new owner
New activity alerts only the owner of an owned lead
Escalations alert the level's audience
One digest per person and team once the oldest alert has waited
FIRSTCALL_DIGEST_SECONDS defaults to 60
A failed digest waits a doubling time
After FIRSTCALL_EMAIL_RETRIES its alerts are marked failed
Email retries default to 3
The email backend defaults to inbox
smtp sends to FIRSTCALL_SMTP_HOST and PORT
The Inbox shows only the plain-text body
Inbox links are server-built lead paths
Each push is checked against current access before sending
Each digest line is checked against current access before sending
The recipient must be active and able to see the lead
Leaving a team cancels only alerts for leads the user can no longer see
Email goes only to an active user of the org
A buyer's address is refused
An address carrying a buyer's phone is refused
Anything but one plain address is refused
Display names and lists are refused
Encoded words are refused
A tray sender is not a buyer; a rescued one is
An allowlist means Firstcall never emails a buyer

The worker pushes right after each job
The scheduler sends pushes escalation queued
A notification opens only this app's pages
FIRSTCALL_PUSH_HOSTS is a list setting with four defaults
A leading dot matches subdomains
https, port 443, never an IP
The host must be on the list
Checked at subscribe
Checked again before every send
The send uses the rebuilt address
Each send waits at most 5 s and reads at most 16 KB
404 or 410 removes the device
FIRSTCALL_PUSH_ALLOW_HTTP is refused in beta
Alert links point at FIRSTCALL_BASE_URL
Beta refuses the local default base URL
Push goes only to the services on FIRSTCALL_PUSH_HOSTS
